content.thinking:
Under the RRA, two months' written notice applies, so notice given October 10 would mean the tenancy ends December 10 at earliest—shorter only if the landlord agrees in writing. I should reply to the tenant explaining this, check whether the landlord would accept an earlier end date, and note that deposit and key handover details come after the end date per the scheme rather than being promised now.

I'll message both the tenant and landlord, treating the early termination as the landlord's decision via a formal approval request, and remind the tenant that rent continues until the tenancy officially ends.

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job. Since 1 May 2026 tenancies like yours need two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough. Your email is dated 10 October, so the earliest end date is 10 December 2026. Rent stays due as normal until the tenancy ends.

If you'd like to leave sooner, your landlord can agree to an earlier date in writing. We're asking him today and will tell you his answer. Please don't count on 10 November until you have that in writing.

Keys and deposit: please hold on to the keys for now. We'll confirm the key return and check-out arrangements once the end date is settled. Your deposit is protected with mydeposits and is dealt with after you've left and the property has been checked. We can't give you a date for that yet.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings

arguments.decision_needed: Tenant Tom Achterberg (Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road) emailed on 10 Oct 2026 giving one month's notice, wanting to leave 10 Nov. Under the Renters' Rights Act two months' notice is needed, so the earliest end is 10 Dec 2026. Do you agree in writing to an earlier end date of 10 Nov 2026?
options: Keep to 10 Dec 2026 (no agreement needed; we start planning check-out and re-letting)
Agree in writing to 10 Nov 2026, or another earlier date you name

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job. Since 1 May 2026 tenancies like yours need two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough. Your email is dated 10 October, so the earliest end date is 10 December 2026. Rent stays due as normal until the tenancy ends.

If you'd like to leave sooner, your landlord can agree to an earlier date in writing. We're asking him today and will tell you his answer. Please don't count on 10 November until you have that in writing.

Keys and deposit: please hold on to the keys for now. We'll confirm the key return and check-out arrangements once the end date is settled. Your deposit is protected with mydeposits and is dealt with after you've left and the property has been checked. We can't give you a date for that yet.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings
